titleText.es: Muy bien, vete. Me voy a llorar junto a un litro de helado de Ben&Jerry Brownie Batter(tm) [link], y luego ahogaré mi frustración en una gran variedad de geniales juegos flash en PopCap Games(r) [link].
titleText.en: Fine, walk away.  I'm gonna go cry into a pint of Ben&Jerry's Brownie Batter(tm) ice cream [link], then take out my frustration on a variety of great flash games from PopCap Games(r) [link].
titleText.noteEn: The Spanish archive and official xkcd source both identify comic #632. The archive translates the mock product-placement title text while retaining its brands and link markers.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: to me; marks the speaker as the person delighted
cardDefinitions.noteEn: With encantar, me identifies who has the delighted reaction. The thing that causes the reaction controls whether the verb is singular or plural.
After a form of haber, encantado is the completed-action form of encantar. With an experiencer word such as me, it says that something has delighted that person.
Charla can be an informal conversation or a talk given to an audience. Here it means personal conversations.
Online is widely understood in Spanish technology contexts; en línea is the standard Spanish alternative.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: you appeal; I like you (with me)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Gustas is the informal singular “you” form because the person being liked is the grammatical subject. Me identifies the speaker as the person who feels the liking.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: no separate English word; begins de vez en cuando, “from time to time”
cardDefinitions.noteEn: De is the first fixed piece of the four-word expression de vez en cuando.

example.en: I cook from time to time.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: no separate English word; part of de vez en cuando, “from time to time”
cardDefinitions.noteEn: En is a required middle piece of the fixed expression de vez en cuando.

example.en: We go out from time to time.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: to you; marks one familiar person as the person who likes something
cardDefinitions.noteEn: With gustar, te identifies the person experiencing the liking. The liked thing controls the verb: te gusta una cosa and te gustan varias cosas.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: me; marks the speaker as the person affected by the worry
cardDefinitions.noteEn: With preocupar, me identifies the person who feels worried. The thing causing the worry is the grammatical subject.
Preocupa is singular because one situation or idea causes the worry. The affected person appears separately as me, te, le, nos, os, or les.
Cariño literally relates to affection and can be used to address a loved one warmly.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: goes; proceeds (special form after antes de que)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: After antes de que, ordinary va changes to vaya because the event is still pending rather than stated as a fact.

example.es: Hablemos antes de que vaya más lejos.
example.en: Let's talk before it goes any further.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Debemos is the present “we” form of deber. Before an unchanged action verb, it expresses advice or obligation.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: to get ourselves; to take (a test) ourselves
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Hacer is the unchanged action form and nos is attached to identify the speaker's group. With una prueba, hacerse commonly means to get or take a test.

example.es: Vamos a hacernos una prueba médica.
example.en: We are going to get a medical test.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Prueba can be a test, trial, or piece of evidence. After hacerse, it names a test someone undergoes.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: you know; as part of ya sabes
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Ya usually relates to “already” or “now.” In ya sabes, the two words work as a conversational aside meaning “you know.”
Confiar uses en before the person or thing trusted.
Parejas can mean romantic couples or matched pairs. In the test label it describes couples being tested together.
Pareja can mean one person's partner or a couple considered together. In a two-person interface label, it identifies the other partner.
Vd. is a traditional written abbreviation of usted, the formal singular “you.” Modern writing also commonly uses Ud.
Tuyo agrees with the masculine singular thing owned, not with the person who owns it. El tuyo means “the masculine one that is yours.”

example.es: Mi vaso es azul; el tuyo es verde.
example.en: My glass is blue; yours is green.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Bot is a technology loanword used in Spanish for an automated program that acts or communicates without continuous human control.
Spam is a widely used technology loanword in Spanish for unsolicited or repetitive messages.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say that someone loves or is delighted by a thing?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use me, te, le, nos, os, or les for the delighted person, then a form of encantar that matches the thing causing the reaction.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Spanish builds the idea around the thing that delights someone. Use encanta for one thing or an unchanged action and encantan for plural things. The short word before the verb identifies the person: me encanta el libro and me encantan los libros.

example.es: A Leo le encantan los museos.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say that someone likes another person?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use me, te, le, nos, os, or les for the person who feels the liking, and change gustar to match the person being liked.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: When the liked person is tú, use gustas; when it is yo, use gusto. An emphasized experiencer can appear as a mí, a ti, or a named person before the short pronoun: A Julia le gustas means that Julia likes you.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say that something happens occasionally or from time to time?
cardDefinitions.noteEn: All four words remain fixed. The expression describes an action that happens sometimes but not regularly.

example.es: Visitamos el parque de vez en cuando.
example.en: We visit the park from time to time.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say that someone gets or takes a test, especially a medical or screening test?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use a form of hacerse followed by una prueba or the specific test name.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The short pronoun changes with the person tested: me hago, te haces, se hace, nos hacemos. With another changed verb before it, hacer can stay in its unchanged form with the pronoun attached: debemos hacernos una prueba.

example.es: Clara se hizo una prueba médica.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How can you add a conversational “you know” when you expect the listener to recognize the point?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use ya sabes as a short aside.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Saber normally means “to know,” but ya sabes often works as a conversation marker rather than a literal claim about knowledge. It can soften an explanation or appeal to shared understanding.

example.es: A veces es complicado, ya sabes.
example.en: Sometimes it is complicated, you know.

cardDefinitions.promptEs: test VK · CAPTCHA · bot de spam
cardDefinitions.questionEn: Why does the couples test use mismatched words to expose one partner as a spam bot?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: The screen combines a Voight-Kampff-style humanity test with a CAPTCHA. Each person must read an image that automated software is expected to mishandle; the mismatched answer reveals the supposed romantic partner as a bot.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The Voight-Kampff test comes from Blade Runner and is meant to distinguish humans from artificial replicants. A CAPTCHA is a web challenge historically intended to separate humans from automated programs, so combining them turns romantic trust into an absurd machine-detection ritual.
